title: Buer shows no brush discharges occur in high vacuum
place_text: NASA electrostatics lab, Kennedy Space Center

tellings.quote: showing that there's no brush discharges in high vacuum conditions

plain: In an electricity lab at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida, tests showed that brush discharges, small spray-like electrical sparks that leak off charged surfaces, do not happen in a strong vacuum. Charles Buhler, a NASA scientist who did the work, describes it first-hand as "showing that there's no brush discharges in high vacuum conditions." He brings it up because it matters to his claim that a push from electric charge alone, which he presents as a kind of antigravity propulsion, is real and not just air leaking sparks.
